meeting_header: Date: 2026-04-21 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes | Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CTO - BrightHealth), Priya Nair (DevOps - BrightHealth), Anika Rao (Security - BrightHealth)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on rollout planning. Reviewed cutover approach (canary -> A/B -> full), monitoring & runbooks, security sign-offs, and next steps for rehearsal and docs. Agreed to dry-run on 2026-04-28 and for Redwood to provide a detailed canary runbook and updated pricing for short-term dedicated burst capacity.
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: All right hi everyone thanks for joining, uh Jordan, Priya, Anika, thanks for making time. We'll run about 40 minutes. Quick agenda: run through cutover approach, canary sizing, monitoring, runbooks, and security open items. Sofia will cover the technical steps.
[00:18] Jordan: Yep sounds good. We're particularly focused on minimal user disruption and having a clear rollback. So canary plus A/B feels right but want details.
[00:30] Sofia: Cool, I'll start — so our recommendation based on the POC is to do a staged rollout: stage 1 small canary (5% of traffic) to Dedicated instance, then expand to 25% with A/B routing for 48 hours, then full cutover if metrics stable. The canary should run long enough to collect 95th and 99th latency and error rates, and compare against baseline.
[00:58] Priya: Quick Q — when you say Dedicated, do you mean Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity or Private (VPC) nodes? We need the difference spelled out because our infra team needs to prep peering and KMS.
[01:12] Ethan: Good call. For the short-term cutover we'd recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved) with a two-week burst option to ensure capacity; the Private deployment is the longer-term plan once compliance sign-off is complete. We'll put both options in the doc.
[01:27] Anika: From security perspective we need KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and proof of data-at-rest encryption. Also SOC 2 evidence for the hosting model.
[01:37] Sofia: Understood. We'll attach the SOC 2 summary and KMS integration requirements. For the canary, the flow is: traffic split at the edge (we prefer doing split via API gateway), route 5% to Redwood endpoint, collect traces and token cost metrics. If error rate > 0.5% or 95th latency exceeds baseline + 200ms we pause and roll back.
[02:03] Jordan: What's the rollback mechanism? Prefer automated rollback on threshold but also manual ops runbook for escalation.
[02:12] Sofia: We support both. The canary runbook defines automated rollback thresholds, plus an ops checklist for manual rollback that includes: cut traffic, switch routing, flush caches, re-point to previous model version, and call the incident channel. We'll send the playbook.
[02:30] Priya: Ok — what monitoring stack do you use? We need hooks into our existing Grafana/Prometheus.
[02:37] Ethan: Redwood Console exposes metrics and a Prometheus endpoint; we can share the Grafana dashboard templates and the tracer hooks. We'll provide dashboard json for your team to import.
[02:48] Anika: Also need RBAC for the Console, SSO/SAML integration plan, and audit log retention config. Who's the contact for that?
[02:57] Ethan: That's me for commercial + Sofia will handle technical pieces. We'll include SSO instructions and retention settings in the security pack.
[03:06] Jordan: Another question on A/B — are you suggesting content-level A/B for prompt variations or infra-level A/B to compare Redwood vs current provider?
[03:16] Sofia: We have two flavors: infrastructure A/B (route a % to Redwood model variant vs current production) to measure latency/cost/quality, and content A/B (same infra but different prompt tuning). For the rollout sequence we're proposing infra-level A/B as stage 2 to validate production characteristics.
[03:34] Priya: For infra A/B we'll need explicit IP ranges and egress rules to allow traffic to Redwood endpoints.
[03:41] Ethan: Noted — we'll include the IP ranges and peering steps.
[03:45] Jordan: Pricing — during the POC the token cost looked ok but we need an option to burst capacity for user surges during cutover.
[03:55] Ethan: We can offer a 2-week dedicated burst pricing option; Sofia will update the pricing sheet with per-token estimates and a fixed reservation for the burst window.
[04:06] Anika: Security sign-off timeline — we need to run our internal security review once you provide artifacts. We expect 5 business days to review SOC2 summary and KMS docs.
[04:16] Ethan: That's fine, we'll aim to deliver docs tomorrow.
[04:19] Sofia: A couple of runbook specifics: checkpointing KV cache — during cutover we recommend warming the KV cache with pre-warmed prefixes to avoid cold-start token cost and latency spikes. Also continuous batching policies should be conservative during the canary to keep latency stable.
[04:40] Priya: How will you measure regressions in quality? We have a prompt test harness and some e2e tests.
[04:48] Sofia: Great — we'll integrate your harness with our eval hooks. We'll run a small set of golden prompts against canary and baseline. If quality delta exceeds threshold (we'll propose 5% drop in exact-match / BLEU-ish metric) we abort. We'll send the thresholds for review.
[05:07] Jordan: Can you do a dry-run or rehearsal so our on-call folks can practice the rollback?
[05:12] Ethan: Yes, we propose a dry-run on 2026-04-28 where we simulate a 5% canary cutover and then force a rollback as a drill. We'll coordinate runbook steps.
[05:22] Priya: For the rehearsal I need the exact commands and route changes so the infra team can script them.
[05:28] Sofia: We'll provide a script and a checklist that includes API gateway commands, k8s ingress adjustments (if any), and curl checks. Note: some transcription here — we had a Kubernetes ingress note in POC that was slightly misnamed as 'kube-ingress' earlier.
[05:46] Anika: A thing on logging — we need traces with request-id propagated back to our systems for audit. Is that in place?
[05:52] Sofia: Yes we support request-id forwarding and provide a trace id in the response headers. We'll show sample logs.
[06:02] Jordan: Any risks you see?
[06:06] Sofia: Main risks: cold start latency if cache not warmed, token-cost spike if batchers misconfigured, and misclassification in prompt tuning causing quality regressions. Mitigations: pre-warm cache, conservative batching, run golden prompts, short canary window with automated rollback.
[06:25] Ethan: Quick commercial recap — Redwood will provide canary runbook, updated pricing including burst option, Prometheus/Grafana dashboards, SSO/SSO docs, SOC2 summary, and we'll schedule dry-run on 2026-04-28.
[06:40] Priya: Sounds good. One minor nit — earlier in the POC we saw a 'token leakage' report; can you include the cost breakdown per route so we can validate unit economics?
[06:51] Sofia: Yep, we'll include token-per-call breakdown and an example cost spreadsheet.
[06:57] Jordan: Ok final question: how do you handle fallback if Redwood region has capacity issues mid-cutover?
[07:05] Sofia: We have smart routing and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant in another region; during canary we'll keep a fallback to the existing provider as a safety net. That requires config of the gateway to switch on error thresholds — we'll show the config snippet.
[07:20] Ethan: Great. Let's list the next steps — I'll follow up with the runbook and pricing by 4/23, Sofia will send dashboards and benchmark data, Priya and Anika will confirm infra and security items.
[07:33] Jordan: Thanks folks. If we can get the docs tomorrow we'll aim for the dry-run on 4/28.
[07:39] Ethan: Perfect thanks everyone. End of call.

Notes: Transcript contains transcription artifacts: 'Redwood Dedicate' sometimes, 'kube-ingress' mention, occasional mis-attributed short lines.
